title: Job records, handover and escalation
audience: Trainees, workers and office staff on the solar panel cleaning track who complete job records, customer handovers and escalations.
learningOutcomes: Complete a standard job record for a PV clean that captures scope, method, observations, exclusions and referrals.
Write a handover that tells the customer what was done, what was excluded and what must be referred.
Use a standard template to reduce repeated admin without removing evidence or checks.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Installing solar panels (last updated 19 October 2026).

instruction.heading: Official sources (start of lesson)
instruction.body: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government (nsw.gov.au), Installing solar panels (page date: Last updated 19 October 2026).

instruction.heading: Why the job record matters
instruction.body: A job record is the evidence of what was agreed, what was checked, what was done and what was referred. It protects the worker and the business in a dispute about damage, a missed exclusion or a warranty question. A record should be complete enough that another person could understand the job without asking the worker.

instruction.heading: The fields a solar job record needs
instruction.body: A standard record should capture the owner and the array owner, the approvals obtained, the scope and exclusions, the array make and model, the instruction source, the method and products, the equipment used, the before and after photographs, the time taken, any defect or unknown, and any referral made. Keep observations and claims in separate fields. Where a field is not applicable or unknown, write so, rather than leaving it blank.

instruction.heading: Using a template to reduce workload
instruction.body: A standard template reduces repeated writing and makes records consistent across jobs. Use fixed fields for the items above, and avoid free text where a choice from a fixed list will do. A template does not remove the checks. Each field must still be completed by a person, and the template must not hide an exclusion, a defect or an unknown. Review the template when the method or the regulations change.

instruction.heading: Customer handover
instruction.body: At handover, give the customer a written summary. It should state what was cleaned, what was excluded and why, any defect observed and who it has been referred to, and any question that is outside the cleaning scope. Do not give a verbal assurance that the panels are compliant, safe, performing or under warranty. Keep a copy of the summary in the job record.

instruction.heading: Escalation
instruction.body: Escalate any electrical, structural, warranty or environmental concern in writing to the owner and to the qualified person named in the procedure. Record who was told, when and what decision is pending. Do not fix a concern on the spot if it is outside the scope, and do not delete a photograph or change a record after it has been made. Corrections are added as dated entries.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant an electrical licence, solar installation licence, accreditation or authority to certify a system. Completing a record template is not a licence or certification.

instruction.heading: Official sources (end of lesson)
instruction.body: Official sources for this lesson (end): NSW Government (nsw.gov.au), Installing solar panels (page date: Last updated 19 October 2026).

procedure: Open the standard job record and complete the owner, array owner and approval fields before the job starts.
Record the scope, the exclusions, the array make and model, the instruction source and the method.
Take before photographs and record the observed condition, separately from any claim.
Record the method, the products, the equipment, the time taken and any unknown.
Take after photographs and record any defect with its position, and record the referral made.
Prepare the written customer handover, stating what was cleaned, what was excluded and what is referred.
Escalate any electrical, structural, warranty or environmental concern in writing, and record who was told.
Sign and date the record, and add any correction as a dated entry rather than changing the original.

workedExamples.situation: A worker finishes a clean and wants to write a handover that says the panels are now fully compliant and will perform at their best.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the handover say instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: Remove the compliance and performance statements. The handover should state what was cleaned, what was excluded, any defect observed with its referral, and that output and warranty questions are outside the cleaning scope. The worker signs and dates the record, and keeps a copy in the job record.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor asks a worker to delete a photograph of a cracked module because it may upset the customer.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not delete the photograph. The record is evidence of what was observed. Keep the photograph, record the defect in writing, and escalate it to the owner and the qualified person. Any correction is added as a dated entry, and the supervisor's request is recorded for the business to review.

equipmentAndPpe: Standard job record template with fixed fields for scope, exclusions, approvals, method and referral
Camera or phone for before and after photographs with dated file names

commonErrors.error: Writing a compliance or performance guarantee in the handover.
commonErrors.prevention: State what was done, what was excluded and what is referred.

commonErrors.error: Leaving fields blank rather than writing unknown or not applicable.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete every field, and mark unknowns as unknown.

commonErrors.error: Deleting or altering a photograph or record.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the original and add any correction as a dated entry.

commonErrors.error: Using a template that auto-completes the checks.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete each field by hand, and review the template when the method changes.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Records must not certify a system as compliant, safe or performing. Record only what was observed and done.
Licence notice: This lesson does not grant an electrical licence, solar installation licence, accreditation or certification authority.

qualityStandard: Every field in the job record is completed, with unknowns and not-applicable items marked.
The handover states what was cleaned, what was excluded and what is referred.
No photograph or record is deleted, and every correction is dated.
Each escalation is in writing, with the person told and the decision pending.
documentationEvidence: Completed job record with owner, approvals, scope, exclusions, method and photographs
Written customer handover with exclusions and referrals
Escalation log with the person told and the date
Dated correction entries where any correction was needed
summary: A complete job record protects the worker and the business.
A template reduces admin, but each check must still be completed by a person.
The close-out note lists the completed work, the excluded items and the matters passed on, and gives no assurance of outcome.
This lesson grants no licence, accreditation or certification authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which record is most useful for a solar clean?
options: A verbal promise that the job is done and the array is clean today
Before-and-after photos, the method, the product and the time
A blank form with the date, the address and the client's name
Nothing, as the job speaks for itself to the customer and the owner

knowledgeChecks.question: A standard job record template helps mainly by:
options: Making the job slower for the crew and the client on site
Removing the need for any checks at all on the job site
Reducing repeated admin while keeping evidence consistent
Hiding exclusions from the customer's view on the form

knowledgeChecks.question: At handover, the worker should:
options: Give the customer a verbal assurance that the panels are compliant with all the rules
Leave without a summary of the work for the customer, the agent or the owner today
Promise energy results for the next few months of the year ahead and beyond
Give a written summary of what was done, what was excluded, and any defect referred

knowledgeChecks.question: An electrical or structural concern is found. What is the correct escalation?
options: Escalate in writing to the owner and a qualified person
Keep it to yourself so the job stays calm and quiet today
Fix it on the spot before the owner returns home tonight
Delete the photo so the file stays tidy and clean today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which template design is consistent with this lesson?
options: Automating scheduling to remove all human checks from the whole job process and the records
Using a record template with fields for scope, exclusions, approvals and defects, reviewed by a person
Using a template that auto-approves unverified work to save time for the team and the office
Hiding defects from the record so the file looks neat and tidy for the owner and the agent
